project.name: VentuSample
project.scope: Offline C++20/Qt workstation for deterministic hip-hop sample generation and PCM16 WAV sample-pack export.

entries.target: Generator failure handling and invalid render inputs
entries.acceptance: Reproduce the defect, isolate its root cause, add a regression check, and verify the corrected behavior at the affected entry point.

entries.target: Generator parameter contracts and user-controlled limits
entries.acceptance: Check boundaries, units, tolerances, rounding and measurement assumptions from more than one independent path.

entries.target: Qt desktop controls and validation feedback
entries.acceptance: Remove the underlying cause across dependent components; do not hide symptoms with local workarounds.

entries.target: Versioned sample-pack manifest and WAV export integrity
entries.acceptance: Close missing acceptance conditions across implementation, tests, documentation, configuration and distribution artifacts.

entries.target: Musical key and mode selection and serialization
entries.acceptance: Exercise the complete user workflow, including invalid input, cancellation, failure and recovery branches.

entries.target: Deterministic variation and seed handling
entries.acceptance: Run deterministic diagnostics for supported platforms and configurations; report unsupported combinations explicitly.

entries.target: Loop, kit, drum and melody generation paths
entries.acceptance: Review functional behavior, security, resource use, accessibility, compatibility and documentation as one change set.

entries.target: Renderer output measurements and audio-quality checks
entries.acceptance: Measure a reproducible baseline before optimizing and prove that correctness, safety and output quality do not regress.

entries.target: CMake targets and CI build variants
entries.acceptance: Restructure components only with explicit interface contracts, migration notes and compatibility regression checks.

entries.target: Main-window state, controls and export workflow
entries.acceptance: Update toolchains, platforms and dependencies deliberately, then run the affected build and regression matrix.

entries.target: User guides, architecture and documented capabilities
entries.acceptance: Synchronize supported profiles, operating modes, locales and configurations so they do not drift independently.

entries.target: Generated-fixture validation and output regression
entries.acceptance: Audit implementation, tests, diagnostics, release workflows and evidence links; record findings with reproducible references.

entries.target: Desktop application entry point and startup lifecycle
entries.acceptance: Recover from partial failures without corrupting existing data; verify idempotency and atomicity where relevant.

entries.target: Project-contract and configuration validation
entries.acceptance: Keep defaults, thresholds, quotas, timeouts and policy boundaries consistent with the documented operating envelope.

entries.target: Quality, monolithic cohesion and rhythm acceptance
entries.acceptance: Verify end-to-end conformance from the public interface through implementation and persisted/exported results.

entries.target: Native C++ generator implementation and interfaces
entries.acceptance: Remove harmful duplication and dependency cycles while preserving public contracts and observable behavior.

entries.target: CI regression matrix for native build and tests
entries.acceptance: Contain failures with explicit upper bounds for memory, CPU, retries, input sizes and execution time.

entries.target: Reaper pack-audit compatibility boundary
entries.acceptance: Resolve mismatches between source code, schemas, APIs, specifications, tests and user-facing documentation.

entries.target: Federation metadata and inter-project schema compatibility
entries.acceptance: Use canonical data formats and versioned interfaces for shared capabilities without erasing project-specific boundaries.

entries.target: Architecture, package export and release acceptance
entries.acceptance: Gate releases on relevant regression checks, clean build artifacts, synchronized documentation and reviewable evidence.

limitations: Evidence checks verify repository-relative file presence only; they do not execute or semantically validate the referenced implementation.
Passing this profile does not certify zero defects, security, hardware compatibility, language parity, audio fidelity or commercial readiness.
The project's existing permissions, licensing, interoperability and safety boundaries remain authoritative.
